newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Zeitler urges strict, lasting EMU controls.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Zeitler urges strict, lasting EMU controls.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler on Tuesday said Europe's planned monetary union must be monitored and controlled on a continual basis and convergence criteria must be adhered to long-term.

In an interview with the Mittelbayerische Zeitung, released ahead of publication on Wednesday, Zeitler said a strict EMU stability pact -- designed to impose sanctions on EU states failing to keep their finances under control -- was essential.
"One year results are not enough to prove commitment to stability, and especially not if they are only the result of 'creative accounting'," he told the newspaper.
Zeitler said the stability pact would help boost cunsumers' confidence in the Euro and should largely function on an automatic basis.
The stability pact, the brainchild of German finance minister Theo Waigel, has been broadly accepted by the European Commission but its details have not yet been finalised.

Earlier on Tuesday, Bundesbank vice president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said in an interview with the Wall Street Journal that the Commission's proposals for a stability pact did not entirely correspond with the German central bank's ideas.
A draft proposal by the Commission suggests that countries running a budget deficit higher than the three percent of GDP demanded by the Maastricht Treaty may face sanctions.
However it is not yet clear which circumstances would allow a country to acceptably exceed specific budget deficit limits.
